page: Microsoft Azure E32as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on x86_64 architecture. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at frequencies up to 3.7 GHz. Cache distribution contains 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory provisioning total is 256.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or bundled local ephemeral storage, relying on external Premium Storage for all disk transactions.

Benchmark measurements indicate strong single-core and cryptographic execution alongside steady multi-core output. The instance achieved 3080.07 in stress-ng single-core testing, complemented by Geekbench scores of 2003.0 for single-core and 16534.0 for multi-core. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic primitives such as AES and SHA-NI, which contributed to an upper-quartile PassMark CPU encryption score of 38547.24. Memory performance tests showed 75.26 GB/sec large-block uncached read throughput and 55.71 GB/sec write throughput, aligning with an above-average PassMark memory score of 2775.75.

From a cost and architectural perspective, the 8:1 memory-to-core allocation provides high memory density without the expense of provisioning unnecessary vCPUs for memory-bound tasks. The lack of local storage requires users to provision network-attached storage, placing disk I/O onto remote data paths. The hardware footprint aligns with large in-memory caches, enterprise relational databases, data transformation pipelines, and memory-intensive analytics workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E32as_v6 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz, paired with 256.0 GB of system memory. Built on x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio for memory-intensive computing. The processor supports advanced instructions including AVX-512 extensions and hardware cryptography, achieving strong results in Geekbench single-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark encryption benchmarks. The instance omits integrated GPUs and bundled local disk storage, depending on external Premium Storage for persistent data. With large-block memory read bandwidth of 75.26 GB/sec and strong multi-threaded decompression throughput, the E32as_v6 is structured for large in-memory caching layers, relational database engines, and memory-heavy enterprise processing.
